title: Preaching poor
hookLine: Dominic's answer to heresy was to live poor and preach well; later Dominicans also served the Inquisition

cards: The pope's envoys rode through the south of France the way important churchmen traveled: good horses, servants, baggage. They'd been sent to win people back from the Cathars, and it wasn't working.
People listened to the envoys, then looked at the Cathar preachers, who went on foot and lived plainly, and compared. The envoys were ready to give up.

Then they met two travelers from Spain, a bishop named Diego and his companion Dominic, and Diego gave them advice they didn't want to hear. Today, that advice, and the harder history that came after it.

teach.h: SEND THE HORSES HOME. GO ON FOOT.
teach.b: Diego's advice, as Jordan of Saxony records it, was blunt. Send the horses home. Go on foot.
Carry no gold or silver. Live and preach as the apostles did, and let people see the Gospel before they hear it.

It's what Jesus tells his disciples in Luke, in the Douay-Rheims: "Carry neither purse, nor scrip, nor shoes." Diego didn't just say it. He sent his own household home and set out on foot, Dominic beside him.
They begged their food, slept where they could, and argued patiently in town squares and at kitchen tables.

teach.h: POOR, SO THEY COULD PREACH WELL.
teach.b: That's the seed of what Dominic later founded: the Order of Preachers, friars who would be poor so they could preach well, and study hard so they could preach truly. Now the harder part, and this path holds it too.
In the generations after Dominic, popes chose Dominican friars, along with Franciscans, to serve as inquisitors: judges in Church courts that tried people accused of heresy.
Those courts used harsh methods, and some of the people they condemned were handed over to the civil authorities and put to death. That's part of the Dominican story, not a footnote to it.
The Catholic Church has since asked God's forgiveness for violence used in the service of truth.
Holding both means not choosing one memory: a bishop who sent his horses home, and the courts that came later, in the same habit.

teach.h: CARRY NEITHER PURSE, NOR SCRIP, NOR SHOES.

how: Dominican friars take vows of poverty, chastity and obedience and give themselves to study and preaching; Dominicans and other Catholics also speak openly today about the order's part in the Inquisition.

o: spreading the Gospel on foot, with no money or comforts
a preacher too unskilled to speak well in public
sermons given only to the poorest people in a town

p: send the horses home, go on foot

s: Diego told the pope's envoys to preach poor, on foot
Jordan of Saxony tells it: no horses, no gold, the apostles' way. Diego went first.
Dominicans had no part in the Inquisition

games.q: you're one of the pope's envoys. your preaching isn't working, and people keep comparing your horses with the plain-living Cathar preachers on foot. what do you do?
o: bring more guards and finer clothes.
send the horses home and preach on foot, poor.
games.why: that was Diego's advice, and he went first, with Dominic beside him. it became the seed of the Order of Preachers.

practice: Open one hand on your lap and place in it Diego and Dominic walking on foot, poor, arguing patiently at kitchen tables; open the other and place in it the courts that came later, the fear, and the people condemned, and breathe with both hands open.
If you pray, pray for the people harmed in the name of faith, and for those who still try to preach poor; if not, just keep both hands open.

wordCard.voice: Preaching poor. Diego and Dominic's answer: no horses, no gold, the Gospel lived before it's spoken. Today's word.

orig.note: Latin: the Order of Preachers, Dominic's name for his friars. it's why they sign OP.

carryVoice: Your line: poor preachers. No horses, no gold: the Gospel seen before it's heard. Rest well.
